title: The first coupling event fails with probability of order one over the logarithm
author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
work: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 886-889: the first coupling event fails with probability of the order one over the logarithm of x. The proof (source lines 891-961) combines four mechanisms that the statement does not mention: the exponential moment bound removes the region in which the level exceeds the iterated logarithm; the failure of the event is then rewritten as a sum over the two parities of the level being close to the logarithm while the corresponding weight is not too small; that condition is in turn shown to force the truncated weighted sum beyond a threshold, where the exponential tail bound applies; and the remaining expectation of a sum over the points of the process is computed with the Mecke equation before the resulting integral is evaluated. The author notes that the argument needs more care than the corresponding step of the paper it refines.
